title: Mixtape and Prom
premise: Wren Amberdale has spent seventeen years perfecting the art of being overlooked, hiding behind his family's bakery counter and baking his grief over his mother's death into sourdough no one questions. When he finds coded instructions tucked inside his grandmother's recipe box, he learns she was one of the founding members of the Harmonists, a secret society that has quietly protected Millbrook's beloved Prom tradition—and its promise that every student, rich or poor, gets one perfect night—for eighty years. Now a school board coup led by Councilman Voss threatens to privatize Prom, and the last living Harmonist is dying. Wren must rally a ragtag crew of outcasts, decode his grandmother's legacy, and pull off an impossible public act of justice before the final audition for the Prom band—choosing truth over loyalty when his best friend's father is the man selling the town out.
about_author: Xanthe Pemberton grew up above her parents' bakery in a small river town where every celebration smelled like butter and sugar. She writes stories about quiet kids who discover that belonging is something you build, not something you're given.

chapters.title: The Quiet Loaf
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet him at 4 a.m., kneading dough shaped like his mother's laugh, invisible in plain sight at Millbrook High. Establishes his survival rules: head down, grades up, locker shut. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sorting grandma Opal's things after her stroke, he finds a card labeled 'Rye for Courage' containing coordinates, dates, and a wax seal—not ingredients. First hint the bakery hid more than bread. Beat: curiosity cracking through fear.

chapters.title: Prom Is Everyone's
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At school, posters announce Prom's 80th anniversary—and a 'modernization proposal.' His best friend Dev Chandra jokes about it; Wren notices Dev's dad, Councilman Voss's business partner, at the meeting. Beat: unease seeded.

chapters.title: The Flour Room
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the first code to a hidden room behind the bakery's original flour cellar, he finds Harmonist records: decades of anonymous scholarships, dress loans, and the Prom Fund. Grandma was a keeper. Beat: awe and vertigo.

chapters.title: Dev Knows Nothing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Dev at home, hearing his father take a call from Voss about 'the venue acquisition.' Dev lies badly to cover what he half-heard. Beat: loyalty beginning to strain under weight it can't name yet.

chapters.title: Audition Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The final audition for the Prom band approaches; Wren secretly plays guitar but never performs. Music teacher Ms. Okafor pushes him to try out. He refuses. Beat: longing versus self-erasure.

chapters.title: Seven Keepers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Decoding further, he learns there were seven Harmonist families; six bloodlines have died out or moved away. He may be the last heir. A dying former Keeper, Ruth Ellery, sends him a summons via flour-dusted envelope. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Tea with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ruth, sharp-tongued and oxygen-tanked, tells him the truth: Voss plans to sell the Grange Hall—the free Prom venue—to a hotel developer. The Harmonists were built for exactly this fight. She asks Wren to be the seventh Keeper. Beat: terror and purpose colliding.

chapters.title: The Outcasts' Table
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Wren recruits the lunch-table misfits: Priya (hacker), Marcus (stagehand), June (seamstress), and reluctantly Dev. Each has been failed by the town's hierarchy. Beat: a found family assembling around a cause bigger than any of them.

chapters.title: Breadcrumbs
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew traces Voss's shell company through permit records while Wren bakes 'message loaves'—recipes with coded scoring—to pass notes undetected. First small victory: they delay a zoning vote. Beat: joy of competence, of mattering.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev discovers his father co-signed the Grange Hall deal. Confronted by Wren, Dev begs for time to fix it inside the family. Wren agrees to wait—a decision that will cost them. Beat: loyalty chosen over truth, knowingly.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Their plan leaks; someone informed Voss. Suspicion poisons the group. June accuses Dev; Dev goes cold. Meanwhile Voss announces the hotel at a press conference, promising a 'premium prom experience.' Beat: betrayal and fracture.

chapters.title: Sourdough Starter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Rock bottom: grounded, suspected, alone in the bakery. Dad finally talks about Mom—and reveals she was a Harmonist too, and knew Wren would find the box someday. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the starter, like the cause, is alive and passed down.

chapters.title: Ruth's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ruth, fading fast, gives Wren the full ledger: eighty years of every kid the Harmonists saved—including Voss himself, once a scholarship boy who now wants to erase the debt. Beat: the villain humanized; justice gets complicated.

chapters.title: Truth or Friend
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wren learns Dev's father forged a signature on the sale documents—but exposing it destroys Dev's family. Dev, cornered, chooses to hand Wren the evidence himself. Beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty fulfilled through truth, not against it.

chapters.title: The Plan at the Grange
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The crew plans a two-front strike: legally challenge the forged deed while staging the most public Prom tradition possible before the vote. They need the whole town watching. Beat: hope with teeth; ticking clock set to audition night.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren auditions after all—with a song his mother wrote, played in the Grange Hall itself, livestreamed by Priya. Half the town tunes in. He speaks the Hall's real history on camera. Beat: invisibility abandoned; voice found.

chapters.title: Voss's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Voss POV sections. Voss moves the council vote up 48 hours and has the Grange condemned on a technicality. Ruth is hospitalized. Everything the crew built teeters. Beat: darkest hour; the machine of power grinding down.

chapters.title: Eighty Years of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. From the hospital, Ruth dictates; Wren reads the ledger aloud at an emergency town meeting—every name the Harmonists ever helped, ending with 'Charles Voss, 1979.' The room turns. Beat: catharsis; justice outside the law, delivered by memory.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. Dev publicly testifies against his father with the forged document. The council voids the sale; the Grange is landmarked. Voss exits in disgrace; Dev's father, broken but not destroyed, begins making amends. Beat: victory earned, not gifted.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Prom happens in the Grange Hall, free for everyone, band fronted by Wren. Ruth attends by ambulance escort; grandma Opal, recovering, dances one slow song. Wren is seen—fully, gladly—for the first time. Beat: belonging achieved.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. Summer: Wren adds a new card to the recipe box—his own handwriting, instructions for the next Keeper. The bakery smells like bread again, not grief. Beat: legacy accepted; the tradition, and Wren, endure.
